grammar_concept.title: Some, Any, Much, Many, A Few, A Little
grammar_concept.rule: Use "some" in positive sentences and offers/requests, "any" in negatives and questions. Use "many" and "a few" with countable plural nouns, "much" and "a little" with uncountable nouns.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: "Some"/"any" indicam uma quantidade indefinida. A escolha entre "many" e "much" depende de se conseguimos contar a coisa (many books) ou não (much time).
grammar_concept.example: I have some money, but I don't have any time. How many books do you have? I don't have much furniture.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Tenho algum dinheiro, mas não tenho nada de tempo. Quantos livros tens? Não tenho muita mobília.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português, "muito/muita/muitos/muitas" concorda com o género e número do substantivo, não com se é contável ou não — isto leva falantes de português a dizer "much people" (em vez de "many people") ou "many information" (em vez de "much information", já que "information" é incontável em inglês). Confundir "some" e "any" também é comum: em português "algum" não muda entre frases afirmativas e negativas como muda em inglês.
grammar_concept.correction: "Many"/"a few" só com substantivos contáveis no plural (many books, a few friends). "Much"/"a little" só com substantivos incontáveis (much time, a little money). "Some" em frases afirmativas e pedidos; "any" em negativas e perguntas: "I don't have any money", "Do you have any questions?"
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Numa loja: "Do you have any batteries? I don't need many, just a few."

vocabulary.definition_en: a small device that stores and provides electrical power
example_sentences: I don't have many batteries left.

vocabulary.definition_en: the ability to wait calmly without becoming annoyed
example_sentences: You need a lot of patience to learn a language.

vocabulary.definition_en: the bags and suitcases that a traveller takes with them (never used with 'a' or in the plural)
example_sentences: How much luggage do you have?

exercises.prompt: Complete: I don't have ___ time to finish this today.
exercises.explanation: "Time" é incontável, por isso usa-se "much", não "many".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "many" com substantivos incontáveis como "time" é um erro comum.

exercises.prompt: Complete: I don't have ___ questions right now.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Manter "some" em frases negativas é um erro comum, já que em português "algum" não muda consoante a frase seja afirmativa ou negativa.

correct_answer: the bags and suitcases that a traveller takes with them (never used with 'a' or in the plural)
exercises.explanation: "Luggage" é incontável em inglês, mesmo sendo "bagagens" muitas vezes usado no plural em português.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. How much luggage did the speaker have?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "I only had a few bags, not much at all."
exercises.transcript: At the airport, the check-in agent asked how much luggage I had. I said I only had a few bags, not much at all.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "Before a long trip, you don't need much luggage — just a few essential things. But you do need a lot of patience at the airport." What do you need a lot of at the airport, according to the text?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "you do need a lot of patience at the airport".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Não tenho muitas pilhas, só tenho algumas."
correct_answer: I don't have many batteries, I only have some.
I don't have many batteries, I just have a few.
exercises.explanation: "Pilhas" (batteries) é contável, por isso usa-se "many", não "much".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "much" em vez de "many" com "batteries" (substantivo contável) é um erro comum.

steps.content: "Many" is pronounced /ˈmeni/ — it rhymes with "penny", not with "rainy". "Much" is /mʌtʃ/, with the same short vowel sound as "cup" or "bus".

steps.prompt: Talk about what you have much/many of and what you have little/few of in your life right now (time, money, patience, free days).
Write 5 sentences about your last trip using some, any, much, many, a few or a little.
